name: Talkdesk Autopilot
operator: Talkdesk (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Talkdesk's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Customer-facing AI agent that resolves requests and completes tasks across voice, digital and email channels, handing over to a human agent when needed.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. Part of the first Portuguese cohort.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

I03.n: Autopilot is configured with no-code tools by operations staff and acts on connected systems such as order management.
I03.span: Powerful no-code tools put you in control.

I08.n: The product page describes Autopilot changing an order's delivery address itself through an integrated order system.
I08.span: it's able to autonomously make the change.

I10.n: Autopilot executes tasks such as refunds and appointment changes through integrations with CRM and ERP systems.
I10.span: By integrating with your CRM and ERP, Autopilot executes tasks

I11.n: Talkdesk states that its AI agents use MCP to call external tools and services of third parties.
I11.span: securely discover, invoke, and exchange information with external tools and services

I12.n: An orchestrator agent identifies intent and passes work to specialised sub-agents, each with its own skills.
I12.span: the orchestrator identifies the customer’s true intent and directs the work to specialized sub-agents

I17.n: Autopilot handles routine queries and passes complex cases that need a person to a human agent.
I17.span: when complex cases are detected that need human empathy and expertise

I19.n: With CXA Operations Center, people watch Autopilot's live interactions and set guardrails while it works on its own.
I19.span: Monitor live interactions, inspect execution behavior, and enforce guardrails

I20.n: The product page states what Autopilot is for: resolving customer requests and completing tasks across channels.
I20.span: agentic AI that resolves customer requests and completes tasks across voice and digital channels

I41.n: CXA Operations Center records session-level execution traces of AI agents for inspection.
I41.span: analyze session-level execution traces, and diagnose failures in production

I47.n: Limits are given to the agent as plain-language instructions, such as when to escalate to a live agent.
I47.span: Escalate to a live agent if the customer mentions a medical emergency

I57.n: Talkdesk publishes a vulnerability disclosure channel for issues affecting its customers.
I57.span: If you find a vulnerability that affects Talkdesk customers, send us a report

I58.n: The data Autopilot draws on is named: Talkdesk Data Cloud interaction history and Knowledge Management content.
I58.span: Leverage the Talkdesk Data Cloud so AI Agents understand history, intent, and sentiment

I65.n: Talkdesk states a strategy of a hybrid workforce of AI agents and human agents on one platform.
I65.span: a hybrid workforce enabled by our platform

I67.n: Autopilot's dashboard shows usage, intents and escalation rate to live agents.
I67.span: Visualize usage, channel distribution, customer intents, and escalation rate to live agents.

S3.n: talkdesk.com publishes an llms.txt (fetched), and docs.talkdesk.com publishes one for its API documentation.
S3.span: # Purpose: AI usage guidance for Large Language Models (LLMs)
